Offline GBC PheWAS mediation follow-up

Author

Gibran Hemani

Published

October 9, 2026

Inventory and local inputs

The report rebuilds from saved associations, with remote extraction, downloads and package installation disabled. Old regional exp_sets, reduced outdat, old MR results and knitr result caches are not inputs to the corrected analysis.

There are 33 unique pairs, 26 mediators and 6 retained target SNPs. The saved follow-up had 53 rows; repeated rows do not add comparisons. The original PheWAS covered eight lead SNPs. The two without retained saved follow-up associations are accounted for below; the saved data do not establish why they were not retained.

These GBC lead variants are not generally weak associations: seven of eight have P < 5e-8; rs2131242 is below that significance threshold (saved outcome P = 9.9e-07). The original report quoted approximately 4.81e-7; the saved outcome association used here differs, and both values are below genome-wide significance. Genome-wide significance alone does not establish instrument validity.

Exact-hit comparisons

Every target estimate uses exactly its named SNP in int_chd, harmonised with the full saved GBC outcome outgwasf. The comparator is rebuilt from that mediator’s saved instruments, excluding the target and ±1 Mb, inclusive, before outcome matching and harmonisation. Saved coordinate mismatches and missing instrument coordinates are excluded. A geographic window does not prove LD independence; there is no fetched LD reference or genome-build conversion. The supplement includes ±2 Mb and additional chromosome 6 25–34 Mb MHC exclusions where relevant.

TwoSampleMR action 3 removes every A/T and C/G palindrome regardless of frequency. Non-palindromic strand complements and allele reversals are harmonised; incompatible alleles, unvalidated proxies, conflicting duplicates and invalid SEs yield explicit unavailability. The recorded target effect allele orients both target associations. A usable total GBC association may remain when a mediator component is unusable.

The exact target uses a Wald ratio. Comparators use a Wald ratio for one instrument or IVW with multiplicative random effects for multiple instruments. Conventional first-order ratio SEs treat exposure effects as fixed; beta/SE-derived F statistics are available in the CSV, and measure strength rather than validity or independence. Decomposition below propagates uncertainty in both multiplicands. Specific mediator transformations/units were not preserved: effects use saved GWAS units, specific unit unavailable, with target and comparator matched by mediator GWAS ID. Comparison panels use their own scales; magnitudes across mediators are not comparable.

Pooled mediator MR

Pooled MR excludes the union of every target locus for each mediator directly from its saved instruments. A SNP excluded for one target cannot return through another target’s complement. This distinct summary is never substituted for the per-target comparator used in decomposition.

Total, indirect and residual direct components

For each pair: t = G→GBC, i = a × b, d = t − i, where a is the exact G→mediator association and b is that target’s other-instruments MR. Components share GBC log-odds units per recorded target effect allele. Opposing signs are retained; missing components are never zero. The pipeline validates t = i + d for every complete pair.

Approximate normal 95% CIs use a first-order delta method with zero covariances: Var(i) = b²Var(a) + a²Var(b), Var(d) = Var(t) + Var(i). General formulas add 2abCov(a,b) to Var(i), and subtract 2bCov(a,t) + 2aCov(b,t) from Var(d). Saved summary data do not identify these covariances. The supplement uses hypothetical equicorrelations −0.3, 0 and +0.3 among a, b and t; these are positive-definite matrices, not estimates of empirical covariance or sample overlap.

These are model-based approximate components, not identified causal natural effects. Binary traits, non-collapsibility, nonlinearity, population differences, LD and instrument validity limit causal interpretation. Indirect effects for separate correlated mediators must not be summed. No mediation percentage is reported.

Interpretation and testing families

Q indicates incompatibility with the common-effect/full-mediation model under its assumptions. Invalid target/comparator instruments, residual LD or population/scale differences may explain incompatibility; Q does not uniquely locate a direct pathway. A non-significant comparison means no detected heterogeneity; mediation unresolved. It proves neither mediation nor equivalence. Comparator precision and instrument strength are recorded in the CSV.

There are 32 BH-incompatible pairs among 33 tested unique pairs in the retained inventory of 33 pairs. Each named family separately applies BH at 0.05 to its available tests; this does not claim global control across separate families. Indirect/residual tests use approximate normal delta-method intervals. The two window/MHC sensitivity scenarios each use their own separately named 33-pair BH family; covariance scenarios describe approximate interval sensitivity. Per-SNP counts describe pair tests and are not additional SNP-level hypothesis tests.

From the repository root, using the existing local data/gbc_phewas_results-g2.Rdata:

Rscript scripts/run-offline-g2.R
quarto render scripts/phewas-followup-g2.qmd --no-cache
Rscript tests/run-tests.R

A compact lossless subset of the required saved associations is included in data/offline-g2-inputs.rds. The source checksums and extraction counts are in Snapshot provenance. No new empirical data were acquired. For a checkout without the original Rdata:

Rscript scripts/run-offline-g2.R data/offline-g2-inputs.rds
GBC_G2_INPUT=data/offline-g2-inputs.rds quarto render scripts/phewas-followup-g2.qmd --no-cache

No remote installation or data access is needed. The older G1 workflow is unchanged. Each render recomputes all tables/figures and bypasses old caches.
